variants.headline: Party divides in two
variants.sub: The colony has seen a party divide into two organisations.
variants.body:
A political party has split in two in {colony}. The division is an organisational fact, not a complete explanation of the differences behind it. In considering {target}, readers should distinguish the break itself from unreported motives, ideological labels or claims about the balance of parliamentary strength.

A party has split in two. A simple sentence for a very public break. There is no need to invent the private quarrel to make it interesting. Readers should ask what the division is for, and whether the people being represented will find something more useful than competing claims to loyalty.

The responsibility of {target} should be considered without presuming the split's cause or its eventual consequences. This account records an organisational division and reserves judgment on particulars not supplied. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
